messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Bethany Cole <bethany@aurorafin.com>

Subject: Aurora Finance POC — headroom & dedicated buffer request

Hi team,

Following the discovery calls last week, Aurora Finance confirmed a short pilot window starting Oct 15. They want to evaluate latency-sensitive scoring for fraud checks (low token counts, high QPS burst). Key asks:

- Temporary dedicated buffer (pilot carve) for Oct 15–29 (2 weeks) to guarantee a baseline of capacity.
- Autoscale policy exception during the window to permit sustained concurrency peaks up to ~16 concurrent inference sessions for the scoring model.
- We will provide a signed term sheet; Aurora is willing to pay for reserved capacity if we can guarantee the headroom.

Numbers (forecast provided in attached plan):
- Baseline steady throughput: 200 qps
- Burst windows (30–90s): up to 1.2k qps
- Preferred reservation: 8 A100-equivalent GPU slots, with burst capability if possible

Attachments: aurora_capacity_plan_v1.xlsx, SLA-draft-Aurora.pdf

I need product/ops confirmation on feasibility and what the ops constraints would be (preemption risk, other pilots impacted). Bethany — adding you for transparency; happy to sync if we need to soften the ask.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying items before I flag this with Capacity & Allocations:

1) Model variant: which model are they targeting for the pilot (name + size)? Is fallback to a smaller/quantized model allowed if capacity gets constrained?
2) Acceptance criteria: p95 latency SLA target, error budget, and demo success metric. We need these to size buffer vs. autoscale.
3) Financial commitment: do they sign a short reservation (two-week paid slot) or do we take a conditional carve with at-risk credits?
4) Region: confirm US-only traffic or multi-region routing needed.

Marcus — can you confirm ops feasibility (what pool we'd pull from, scheduling/preemption impact, and the narrowest exception we can grant to autoscale)? Neha — loop in compliance if there are any logging/audit changes required for a carveout.

If we can get those answers today, I can provisionally approve a conditional carve for Oct 15–29 and open an ops ticket to lock slots pending legal/finance sign-off.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Quick ops readout:

- We have a pilot pool in us-west with ~120 GPU slots available during that period. Carving 8 A100-equivalent nodes for two weeks is possible but will reduce slack for other pilots.
- Autoscale policy: our default policy enforces per-customer burst caps and global pool fairness. We can grant a timeboxed exception to bump the cap for DEAL-2026-AUR-17, but it will require an override ticket and an explicit rollback schedule.
- Fallback: if Aurora accepts fallback to a quantized/redwood-v1-quant variant, effective capacity increases ~2.5x; latency will likely increase by ~15–20% in worst cases. Good low-risk mitigation.
- Ops items I need: formal reservation form (resource sku + duration + priority), target model name, and a contact for any on-call escalations during the window.

Short answer: feasible with the exception and the right paperwork. I'll prepare cost/impact numbers once I have the reservation form.

—Marcus

Team — decision and next steps: provisional approval granted for the Oct 15–29 window with the following constraints and actions. This is timeboxed and conditional on legal/finance sign-off (SOW + PO).

Decision details:
- Reserve: 8 A100-equivalent GPU slots in us-west for Oct 15 00:00 → Oct 29 23:59 (local).
- Autoscale exception: increase per-customer burst cap to allow up to 16 concurrent inference sessions for DEAL-2026-AUR-17 for the timeboxed window. Exception will be implemented by ops and auto-revoked at 23:59 on Oct 29.
- Fallback: allow automatic fallback to redwood-v1-medium-4bit during spikes; routing policy should prefer redwood-v1-medium-fp16 unless latency/SLA likely to be violated.

- Marcus: open ops override ticket and provision reservation; add rollback automation; estimate marginal cost and share with Finance by EOD 10/06. (owner: marcus_lin)

- Jonas: review final SOW and sign-off for go/no-go by 10/08. (owner: jonas_weber)

I've set the provisional carve on the Capacity calendar pending Marcus's ops ticket. Bethany — expect a short SOW from Jonas's team for signature; Laura will coordinate the PO.

I'll close out here once ops ticket and SOW are in place. Thanks everyone for the quick turn.
